sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cnabetius was a god of the Continental Celts. His name is translated as the crippled one, but records say little about him. Inscriptions from the Celtic lands of Germany and Austria bear his name. The Romans linked him to their warrior god Mars. Scholars place him among wounded kings such as the Irish Nuada.

okr.objective: Cnabetius is a scantily known Continental god whom the Romans tied to Mars.
key_results: Inscriptions name him in Germany and Austria.
